driver.label: driver
driver.sources: Unchanged from the original driver-only envelope of issue 14621: tour-labelled driver launch spin for face-to-path 10-15 degrees stays under about 3500 rpm. TrackMan tour averages put the driver near 2,500 rpm, so the cap sits well above a normal strike and only trips on an impact-solver artefact.

wood.label: wood
wood.sources: Fairway woods share the driver envelope by decision of issue 15443 (driver and wood behaviour unchanged). The TrackMan tour average 3-wood launch spin is about 3,700 rpm, so this cap is conservative for woods and refuses rather than shows a doubtful flight.

hybrid.label: hybrid
hybrid.sources: TrackMan tour average hybrid launch spin is about 4,400 rpm; the cap adds a margin of about 25 percent (4,400 x 1.25 = 5,500). It lies between the wood and the iron envelope, as the club does.

iron.label: iron
iron.sources: TrackMan tour averages: 7-iron 7,097 rpm, 9-iron 8,647 rpm. The cap is the 9-iron average plus a margin of about 15 percent (8,647 x 1.15 = 9,944, rounded to 10,000), so a 7-iron near 7,500 rpm is valid and the shortest iron is still inside. Long irons (3-iron near 4,600 rpm) share this one cap; it is permissive for them by design, since the class is decided by the club name and the model has no per-number envelope.

wedge.label: wedge
wedge.sources: TrackMan tour average pitching wedge launch spin is about 9,300 rpm; wedges spin more as loft rises (sand and lob wedges reach roughly 10,000 to 11,000 rpm on tour). The cap is the pitching wedge average plus a margin of about 35 percent (9,300 x 1.35 = 12,555, rounded down to 12,500).

club_name_patterns.sources: Wedge names and the usual two-letter abbreviations, matched on a lowercase club name.
Hybrid names and numbered forms such as 4h or h4.
Iron names and numbered forms such as iron7, i7 or 7i.
Driver names and the one-wood abbreviation.
Fairway wood names and numbered forms such as 3w or w3.
